package_info.why_malicious: The app collects and transmits sensitive user data (including precise location and PII) to remote servers without user consent, uses unencrypted communications exposing all data to interception, allows account takeover due to broken authentication, and exposes Bluetooth GATT characteristics for arbitrary command injection, enabling device manipulation and denial of service.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /api/dmap-analysis-point-server/v2/insertBaseBurialPointInfoV2 HTTP/1.1
Host: prod.api.app.d-map.cn
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

[{"appVersion":"2.4.1","imei":"629*","latitude":"40.*","longitude":"-8.*","userId":1043065036087934976,...}]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app collects device identifiers and precise GPS coordinates, then sends this data in plaintext via HTTP POST to a remote server in China, exposing user location and PII.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Transmitting precise location and device identifiers to a remote server without user consent is a major privacy violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps should only transmit necessary data, with user consent, and always over encrypted channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Location-based services may send anonymized, consented location data for navigation or weather apps.
key_indicators: Transmission of GPS coordinates and IMEI
No user registration required for data exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app sends user registration and authentication data (including email and password) in plaintext over HTTP, exposing credentials to any network observer.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Transmitting credentials and PII over unencrypted HTTP exposes users to credential theft and account hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps must use HTTPS/TLS for all sensitive data transmission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; credential transmission must always be encrypted.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app allows password reset for any userId without authentication, enabling account takeover by anyone who knows a userId.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Lack of authentication or authorization on password reset endpoint allows trivial account hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require proof of identity (token, email verification) for password changes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; password reset must always be authenticated.

execution_context.file_location: BLE pairing handler in app/watch firmware

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Pairing is confirmed by simple hand movement or button press, with no timeout or user validation.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the watch allows BLE pairing with any device upon simple hand movement, with no timeout or user validation, enabling unauthorized pairing.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Lack of pairing validation allows attackers in proximity to pair and control the device.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal BLE devices require explicit user confirmation and timeouts for pairing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fitness trackers may use simple pairing, but should require explicit user action.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Write Command (0x52) to Handle: 0x0022, Value: 2301093127800360affd6d696e679b (spoof call)
Write Command (0x52) to Handle: 0x0022, Value: 230109311d01010a01180788015200 (set alarm)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app (or any paired device) can write arbitrary data to GATT handle 0x0022, triggering spoofed incoming calls or setting persistent alarms on the watch.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unrestricted write access to GATT characteristics allows attackers to manipulate device behavior, causing denial of service or social engineering attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal BLE devices restrict sensitive GATT writes to authenticated/authorized apps.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may set alarms or notifications, but only after secure pairing.

attack_chain.action: App collects device identifiers and GPS location, sends to remote server in China over unencrypted HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: PII and location exfiltration, user tracking

attack_chain.action: App transmits user credentials and registration data in plaintext over HTTP.
Attacker exploits password reset API to take over any account using only userId.
Attacker pairs with watch using simple hand movement, no user validation or timeout.
Attacker writes to BLE GATT handle to spoof calls or set persistent alarms, causing denial of service or social engineering.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device manipulation, user harassment, denial of service

behavioral_signatures: Unencrypted HTTP POSTs containing GPS coordinates and device identifiers
Unencrypted HTTP POSTs/GETs with user credentials or PII
Password reset API calls lacking authentication
BLE pairing events without user confirmation or timeout
BLE GATT writes to handle 0x0022 with alarm/call payloads
file_indicators: Android app with excessive permissions (location, contacts, SMS, audio, etc.)
BLE GATT characteristic 0x0022 accessed for write operations
network_indicators: Unencrypted HTTP traffic containing location, IMEI, or credentials
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unencrypted HTTP traffic from the app to prod.api.app.d-map.cn containing GPS, IMEI, or user credentials. Flag password reset API calls that lack authentication. Detect BLE pairing events that occur without explicit user confirmation or timeout. Monitor BLE GATT writes to handle 0x0022 for alarm or call spoofing payloads. Review app permissions for excessive or unnecessary access to sensitive data.
